# Jeremiah 12 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** LORD, You always prove to be right when I bring a complaint to You. But let me raise one concern: Why do wicked people prosper? Why do dishonest people have such easy lives?

**2** You planted them, and they've taken root and flourished. They talk about You, but their hearts are far from You.

**3** But You know my heart, LORD. You see me and test my devotion to You. Drag these people away like sheep to be butchered! Set them aside for the day of slaughter!

**4** How long must this land mourn? Even the grass in the fields has dried up. The animals and birds have disappeared because of the wickedness of the people who live here. They say, "God doesn't see what will happen to us."

**5** The LORD replied, "If racing against people has worn you out, how will you race against horses? If you stumble on open ground, what will you do in the tangled jungle along the Jordan?

**6** Even your own brothers, your own family, have turned against you. They've joined the mob calling for your blood. Don't trust them, no matter how nicely they speak to you."

**7** "I have abandoned My people, My special possession. I have surrendered My beloved ones to their enemies.

**8** My chosen people have roared at Me like a lion in the forest, so I have treated them with contempt.

**9** My chosen people act like a speckled vulture, but vultures are circling around to attack them. Go, gather the wild animals to come and feast!

**10** Many rulers have ravaged My vineyard, trampling down the plants, turning My beautiful land into a barren wasteland.

**11** They've made it desolate — the barren land cries out to Me. The whole country lies empty, and no one seems to care.

**12** Destroyers sweep across the barren hilltops, for the sword of the LORD devours the land from one end to the other. No one will be left in peace.

**13** My people have planted wheat but harvest thorns. They've worn themselves out for nothing. They will harvest shame instead of grain, because of the LORD's fierce anger."

**14** Now this is what the LORD says about the hostile nations who seized the land He gave to His people Israel: "I will uproot those nations from their lands, and I will pull Judah out from among them.

**15** But afterward I will have compassion on them and bring each one home to their own inheritance, their own land.

**16** And if these nations truly learn the ways of My people — if they learn to make their vows in My name, saying 'As the LORD lives,' just as they once taught My people to swear by Baal — then they will be accepted and given a place among My people.

**17** But any nation that refuses to obey will be completely uprooted and destroyed," declares the LORD.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **12:1**: Jeremiah does something incredibly bold — he challenges God's justice to His face. And God doesn't rebuke him for it. The Bible makes room for honest wrestling with God.

- **12:5**: God's answer is basically: 'You think this is hard? It's about to get much worse.' Sometimes God doesn't remove our pain — He builds our capacity to endure it.

- **12:7**: One of the most heartbreaking verses in the Bible — God says He has abandoned the thing He loves most. God's judgment isn't cold or detached; it costs Him deeply.

— PNEUMA
